{{Short description|Algebraic number field unit}}
In mathematics, a '''cyclotomic unit''' (or '''circular unit''') is a [[unit (ring theory)|unit]] of an [[algebraic number field]] which is the product of numbers of the form (ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=''a''}}&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1) for ζ{{su|b=''n''}} an ''n''<sup>th</sup> [[root of unity]] and 0 < ''a'' < ''n''.

==Properties==
The cyclotomic units form a subgroup of finite [[Index of a subgroup|index]] in the [[Dirichlet's unit theorem|group of units]] of a [[cyclotomic field]].  The index of this subgroup of ''real'' cyclotomic units (those cyclotomic units in the maximal real subfield) within the full real unit group is equal to the [[Class number (number theory)|class number]] of the maximal real subfield of the [[cyclotomic field]].<ref>Washington, Theorem 8.2</ref>

* If {{mvar|n}} is the power of a prime, then {{math|1=ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=''a''}} − 1}} is not a unit; however the numbers {{math|1=(ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=''a''}} − 1)/(ζ{{su|b=''n''}} − 1)}} for {{math|1=(''a'', ''n'') = 1}}, and ±ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=''a''}} generate the group of cyclotomic units. 

* If {{mvar|n}} is a [[composite number]] having two or more distinct prime factors, then {{math|ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=''a''}} − 1}} is a unit. The subgroup of cyclotomic units generated by {{math|1=(ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=''a''}} − 1)/(ζ{{su|b=''n''}} − 1)}} with {{math|1=(''a'', ''n'') = 1}} is not of finite index in general.<ref>Washington, 8.8, page 150, for ''n'' equal to 55.</ref> 

The cyclotomic units satisfy ''distribution relations''. Let {{mvar|a}} be a rational number prime to {{mvar|p}} and let {{math|''g''<sub>''a''</sub>}} denote {{math|exp(2''πia'') − 1}}.  Then for {{math|1=''a'' ≠ 0}} we have {{nowrap|<math display="inline"> \prod_{p b=a} g_b = g_a</math>.}}<ref>Lang (1990) p.157</ref>

Using these distribution relations and the symmetry relation {{math|1=ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=''a''}} − 1 = −ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=''a''}} (ζ{{su|b=''n''|p=−''a''}} − 1)}} a basis ''B''<sub>''n''</sub> of the cyclotomic units can be constructed with the property that {{math|''B''<sub>''d''</sub> ⊆ ''B''<sub>''n''</sub>}} for {{math|''d'' {{!}} ''n''}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://perisic.com/cyclotomic | title = Marc Conrad's Cyclotomic Units}}</ref>
